_meta.source: FIESTA tax engine v1.0 — compute_tax_25_26() with dual-track foreign-15%-cap + local-progressive (CEO directive 2026-05-20)
_meta.note: Illustrative cases anonymised from Lanka.tax foreign-income filer profiles. Names + NIC redacted. Numbers are engine-computed against the new 25/26 dual-track slabs (Rs 1.8M relief + Rs 1M @ 6% shared first band + foreign 15% cap above + local 18/24/30/36 progressive above). Pro-rata split of the shared first band by source — Phase 6 optimum-allocation refinement deferred per CEO directive.
_meta.engine_provenance: compute_tax_25_26 in fiesta/tax/engine.py, slabs in fiesta/tax/data/slabs.yaml
_meta.ceo_sign_off_required: These savings depend on the customer's actual deduction stack being audit-defensible. Numbers are representative, not promises.

examples.persona_short: SL software developer, USD 80K from US client
examples.persona_long: Anjana D. (anonymised), 31, married, 1 child. Self-employed software developer based in Colombo, billing one US-based client USD 6,667/month (USD 80K/year). Works from home office (separate room) on co-rented apartment Rs 90K/month. All income foreign-sourced.
deductions_claimed_with_fiesta: Home-office portion of rental (50% of Rs 90K × 12 = Rs 540K)
examples.note: Foreign-income saving = deductions × 15% (the foreign cap rate). Real saving honest under 25/26 rules — not the Rs 1.91M or Rs 540K previously circulated; those assumed the wrong bracket structure.

examples.persona_short: SL designer, EUR 45K mix-clients, subcontractor cousin
examples.persona_long: Priya S. (anonymised), 28, single. Graphic + brand designer, freelances for 4 EU clients totalling EUR 45K/year. Outsources illustration to cousin (related party) for EUR 8K/year — DEFAULT-ON related-party disclosure included in FIESTA-generated Service Agreement. All income foreign-sourced.
deductions_claimed_with_fiesta: Subcontractor fees to cousin (Rs 2.6M) — related-party disclosure + arms-length pricing memo attached
examples.note: FIESTA's §195 DEFAULT-ON disclosure shields the cousin payment from audit-time challenge. Foreign-income saving = 3.24M × 15% = 486K.

examples.persona_short: SL accountant, AUD 60K mix (employer + own clients)
examples.persona_long: Nuwan F. (anonymised), 42, married, 2 kids. Senior accountant on AUD 36K retainer with Australian firm + own Sri Lankan client base (Rs 1.8M domestic). Rents home office, claims insurance + ICASL CPD. Mix-source income — 87% foreign, 13% local.
examples.note: Mix-source filers: pro-rata split of the shared first Rs 1M band + 15% on foreign above + progressive on local above. Phase 6 optimum-allocation refinement (allocate first band to local-first for higher saving) will boost this figure in v1.1.
